record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometry and Topology
record.original_question: For an integer k > 2, let X be a smooth, compact manifold of real dimension 2k that admits an almost complex structure. Must X admit some complex-manifold structure, not necessarily homotopic to the given almost complex structure?

evidence.quote: If k > 2, does every smooth, compact, 2k-dimensional manifold which admits an almost complex structure have the structure of a complex manifold? (The almost complex structure as a complex manifold need not to be homotopic to the given one.)

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $k>2$ be an integer, and let $X$ be a smooth compact manifold of real dimension $2k$. Recall that an almost complex structure on $X$ is a smooth bundle endomorphism $J\colon TX\to TX$ with $J^2=-\mathrm{id}$, and a complex-manifold structure on $X$ is an atlas of charts into $\mathbb{C}^k$ whose transition maps are holomorphic. Suppose $X$ admits an almost complex structure. Must $X$ admit some complex-manifold structure? (The complex structure is not required to induce an almost complex structure homotopic to the given one.)
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of whether every compact almost complex manifold of real dimension 2k>4 admits a complex-manifold structure is widely cited as an open problem in differential and complex geometry (related to Yau's problem list and the classical Hopf problem; the dimension-6 case includes the still-unresolved S^6 question). No proof or counterexample is known in general.

status_evidence.title: Almost complex manifold - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Whether an almost complex structure implies the existence of a complex structure is much less trivial, and not true in general.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of a complex structure given an almost complex structure is a nontrivial, generally unresolved question.

status_evidence.title: Almost Complex Structures and Obstruction Theory (Albanese)
status_evidence.snippet: Notes discuss obstructions to integrability and the open status of existence of complex structures on almost complex manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: The integrability/existence problem in higher dimensions remains open.

status_evidence.title: On the history of the Hopf problem
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the Hopf problem on whether S^6 admits a complex structure, still open.
status_evidence.claim: The dimension-6 instance (S^6) of the problem remains open.
